title: What Actually Gets Hotter Than the Sun During Lightning?
post_title: What Actually Gets Hotter Than the Sun During Lightning? | QuantaTale
post_description: The famous lightning temperature fact needs one important correction. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-temperature https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/lightning/sound-of-thunder #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: People say lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun. More precisely, a lightning channel can heat the nearby air to roughly 54,000 degrees Fahrenheit in a fraction of a second. The lightning flash rapidly heats that air, making it expand explosively. That expansion creates a shock wave that we hear as thunder. So the extreme temperature refers to the heated air around the lightning channel—not a claim that the entire bolt is a hot solid object.
